mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances following GDPC1 declines, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased cost pressures on businesses.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last two months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is a major driver of economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to potential economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 4%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
